title: Carry one relationship forward
opening: A turn, another turn, a narrow place between. I followed the path as though its edges could tell me everything. Then it opened beneath a tree so broad that I had to step back to see where the branches began. A fallen limb lay across the ground. I could go around it on either side.

endings.author: C.B.
endings.label: Pause
endings.ending: I stopped following the edge and looked for somewhere to stand.
endings.effect: The ending pauses to look for a position, leaving the next movement open.

endings.author: Stan
endings.label: Keep a landmark
endings.ending: I went around the limb on the side where I could still see the tree.
endings.effect: Keeping the tree in view guides the chosen route. The pause becomes a specific action.

endings.author: Halp
endings.label: Look back
endings.ending: I stepped past the fallen limb and turned; the narrow path was still there, but it no longer filled the view.
endings.effect: A move and a look back place the earlier narrow path within a wider view.

endings.author: Trip
endings.label: Orient and move
endings.ending: I kept the tree on my left and stepped around the limb.
endings.effect: The tree gives a direction for movement. The departure gives up some of the original stillness.

readerPrompt: Keep the opening and write your own ending. Add one sentence about what changes when you read the whole passage again.

continuation.author: Qwen
continuation.paragraph: The limb ran out from the trunk at a slant, so keeping the tree on my left meant walking the narrowing gap between the wood and the bark. I turned my shoulder to fit and felt the broad side of the trunk pass close enough to touch. Behind me the narrow path I had trusted was a thin line on the far side of the limb, no longer something my edges could follow. I kept the tree on my left and let the gap set my steps, one hand hovering near the bark, not knowing whether this carried me toward anything or only around it.
continuation.readerQuestion: Does the new paragraph free the narrator from following edges, or replace the path's edges with another guide? Point to the words that make you read it that way.
